links.comparator_used: Untuned (off-the-shelf) AnonCAT without concept alignment or fine-tuning
links.outcome: Word-level PII classification F1 (de-identification) on site-specific data
links.effect: AnonCAT F1 increased from 0.851 (0.843-0.859) to 0.910 (0.905-0.914) after fine-tuning; fine-tuned precision 0.978 (0.973-0.982), recall 0.850 (0.843-0.858); least performance shift across datasets
links.tradeoff: Fine-tuned AnonCAT recall (0.850) was lower than the best tool, Azure DeID (0.950), despite high precision; fine-tuning requires site-specific annotated data
links.quote: AnonCAT showed significant improvement in performance on fine-tuning (F1 increase from 0.851; 0.843-0.859 to 0.910; 0.905-0.914).

links.comparator_used: Zero-shot prompting of general-purpose LLMs for de-identification
links.outcome: De-identification performance and hallucinated or added text in LLMs with 1, 5, 10 in-context examples
links.effect: GPT-4-0125 with ten shots reached F1 0.898 (0.876-0.915), precision 0.874, recall 0.924; hallucinatory output persisted in Phi-3-mini and Llama-3-8B at zero-, one- and five-shots, and universally for Gemma-7b-IT
links.tradeoff: Few-shot examples did not remove hallucination in all models; Gemma-7b-IT hallucinated at every shot count; zero-shot figures for direct comparison were not given in the abstract
links.quote: Low-adaptation strategies may improve the performance of generalist LLMs and task-specific models.

design_hint: local fine-tuning and few-shot adaptation with site-specific data
